entries.core_move: Verify additivity for a continuous-time input-output system by comparing the output produced by a summed input with the sum of the outputs produced by each input separately.
Verify homogeneity by testing whether a continuous-time system that maps $x(t)$ to $y(t)$ also maps any scaled input a $x(t)$ to the scaled output a $y(t)$ as part of linearity.

Apply the superposition test to a continuous-time input-output system by combining additivity and homogeneity to decide whether scaled-and-summed inputs produce the matching scaled-and-summed outputs.

entries.lesson_title: Testing Linearity from a System Rule
entries.core_move: Apply the superposition test to a continuous-time input-output system rule by comparing its response to a scaled sum of inputs with the scaled sum of the individual responses to decide whether the rule is linear.
Verify that differentiation-based continuous-time input-output rules are linear by applying additivity and homogeneity through the superposition test.

Classify constant offset systems by applying the superposition test to a continuous-time input-output rule and recognizing that an added output offset breaks homogeneity and the zero-input, zero-output condition.

Test a continuous-time squaring system for linearity by computing its outputs for summed and scaled inputs and identifying the cross-term or squared-scale mismatch that violates additivity and homogeneity.

Classify continuous-time input-output systems as linear or nonlinear by applying additivity, homogeneity, and the superposition test to system rules such as derivative, constant-offset, and squaring operations.
